status: Implementation plan; this file is not an available lesson
objective: Separate radial and tangential acceleration and use actual forces to sustain a circular path with constant or changing speed.
preparation: m03-l01 force inventories and unilateral contact

conventions.coordinates: Fixed x right, y up. Angle theta increases counterclockwise from +x and uses radians in derivatives.
conventions.motion: For fixed radius r>0, v=r omega e_theta and a=-r omega² e_r+r alpha e_theta. Speed is r|omega|.
conventions.tangential: The signed e_theta component r alpha differs from the rate of change of nonnegative speed when omega<0. At a reversal, do not assume the derivative of speed is two-sided.
conventions.force: Centripetal describes the inward component of the net force. It is not an additional interaction.

teachingSequence: Relate arc length, radians, signed angular velocity, speed, and the positive period for uniform nonzero rotation.
Differentiate the position vector, including the changing unit vectors, to derive radial and tangential terms.
Resolve total acceleration and distinguish constant speed from constant velocity.
Use real force inventories for a flat friction-supported circle and a frictionless bank.
Choose inward axes at the top and bottom of a vertical circle; solve the support constraint and check its sign.
Distinguish a local top-of-loop contact condition from the later energy question of whether the top can be reached.

workedFixtures.expected: At theta=0, v=(0,-6) m/s while a=(-18,2) m/s². Speed is decreasing because v dot a<0.
|omega|=2 rad/s and T=pi s; speed nonzero, radial acceleration=12 m/s².
Required inward normal=8 N; at speed sqrt(20) m/s it is zero; at 4 m/s the required -2 N is impossible and contact is lost.
Upward inward normal=28 N. Gravity is outward relative to the center at the bottom.
Minimum ideal static coefficient=1/2. Required radial force per kg is 5 N/kg.
Design speed=10 m/s and normal magnitude=20sqrt(2) N.

oracles: Differentiate Cartesian position independently using centered finite differences.
Check r dot v=0, r dot a=-|v|², and orthogonal acceleration norms.
Project actual forces into radial and tangential axes and verify both component equations.
Check zero speed, both rotation directions, zero tangential acceleration, contact equality, and impossible support.

investigation.type: Instantaneous-state simulation with a vertical circular track and an explicit tangential actuator
investigation.reasoning: Predict inward radial acceleration, total acceleration magnitude, required inward normal force, and contact feasibility.
investigation.normalConstraint: For an object inside the circular track, N_required=m(v²/r-g sin(theta)). The track can push inward, not pull outward.
investigation.tangentialActuator: To prescribe a_theta, the actuator must supply F_theta=m a_theta+mg cos(theta). State this explicitly rather than silently imposing nonuniform speed.
investigation.infeasibleCase: Display the target circular kinematics as infeasible when N_required<0. The actual normal is zero; do not present the prescribed circular path as the ensuing trajectory.
investigation.accessibility: Keyboard number inputs and quarter-turn controls; vector directions with labeled magnitudes; a complete component table. Distinguish diagram direction arrows from any quantitative arrow-length scale.
investigation.persistence: State that exploratory controls reset; save comparisons in lesson notes. Practice and checkpoint snapshots use the existing persistent store.
